claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about your son Alex, who is 11 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This typically means either you live with him, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with things like clothes, food, and other expenses for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess whether your contributions would qualify you for Child Benefit, I need to understand more:

**Do you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards Alex's upkeep? Currently, Child Benefit is £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child (or £16.95 per week for additional children). Do your contributions for food, clothes, and other expenses meet or exceed this amount?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute £26.05 per week towards Alex's upkeep, so that does meet the requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand Alex's living situation:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and how long has he been living with them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with someone else in their household.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand Alex lives with someone else. To properly assess your eligibility, I need a bit more detail:

**Is the person Alex lives with claiming Child Benefit for him, or has anyone else made a claim for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the person he lives with isn't claiming Child Benefit for him. No one else has made a claim for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just to confirm a few final details:

**How long has Alex been living with this other person? Has it been more or less than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living with them for quite a while now - it's been more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me make sure I have everything correct:

**Just to confirm - you make regular contributions of £26.05 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit amount), and you've been making these contributions consistently since he moved to live with the other person. Is that correct?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. I've been making these regular contributions of £26.05 per week towards his upkeep.

conversation.text:
**Good news! Based on the information you've provided, you appear to be ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 11 years old, which is under the age limit of 16 (or 20 if in approved education/training)
- You live in the UK
- Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're making regular contributions of £26.05 per week towards his upkeep, which exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the rules, you can still get Child Benefit for a child who lives with someone else if you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep (including things like food, clothes, and other expenses). Since you're meeting this requirement, you should be eligible to claim.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

Would you like any additional information about how to make your claim?
